anya.sec: ALERT: artifact-scan found embedded credentials in model artifacts and pipeline outputs stored in our internal artifact registry (artifactory/model-store). This is a company-wide advisory — we must rotate any tokens that were used to push artifacts and start enforcing artifact signing for model and container uploads. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/artifact-signing-and-scanning :warning:

artifact-bot: artifact-scan v3 results: 46 artifacts with probable secrets (AWS keys, GCP SA keys, Azure app secrets) discovered in model checkpoints and release tarballs, 12 artifacts authored by infra-ci pipelines, 8 artifacts published by user repos with no owner metadata. Top repos: research/large-ckpt, experiments/llm-tuning, infra/tools. Full report: https://redwood.internal/reports/artifact-scan-2118000001 (sensitive link)

pj.platform: how severe? are these live creds?

artifact-bot: Severity matrix: 14 are high (long-lived keys detected and validated against cloud logs), 20 medium (likely keys; need confirmation), 12 low (false positives or expired tokens). Some keys are active (last seen used to call AWS STS or GCP IAM within last 7 days).

anya.sec: Immediate actions (short):
1) Security will revoke any confirmed active keys found in artifacts and notify owners.
2) All teams must rotate tokens used by CI/publish pipelines and re-push artifacts with new credentials.
3) Starting 2026-09-01 we will require artifact signing for model & container pushes; unsigned artifacts will be quarantined by the registry.
4) Add owner metadata to your artifact pushes (team, owner-email) in your publish workflow.

ci-bot: CI helper: to add owner metadata and sign push, update your pipeline to call `sigstore`/`cosign` before upload. Example (GitHub Actions):
```
- name: Sign artifact
  run: |
    cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY_PATH registry.redwood.internal/model-store/repo:tag
- name: Upload
  run: |
    curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARTIFACT_TOKEN" --data-binary @artifact.tar.gz https://registry.redwood.internal/model-store/repo/...
```

anya.sec: For quick mitigation: if your pipeline uses long-lived service tokens, migrate to OIDC or ephemeral CI roles. If you need a short script to find tokens used by a repo, run: `python tools/find_embedded_secrets.py --path artifacts/ --pattern "AKIA|AIza|client_secret" --output findings.csv` and open a ticket with the CSV.

pj.platform: will this quarantine break downstream deployments that pull these artifacts? We need a migration path and a temporary grace period for production routes.

anya.sec: Quarantine behavior: registry will set artifact state to QUARANTINED if unsigned or containing flagged secrets. Pulls for quarantined artifacts return 403. Grace for production: artifacts with `owner:team` and `critical:true` metadata will be given a 14-day grace window once policy is enabled; teams must re-sign and re-push within that window. For obvious breakages file `sec-artifact-hold` ticket.

ops-lead: can security provide per-team CSV of impacted artifacts and owner emails so we can bulk-ticket?

artifact-bot: CSV export queued. API: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.internal/artifacts?filter=secrets&format=csv"` Results will DM platform/ops leads in 15m.

talia.sre: sample remediation steps for model owners?

anya.sec: Remediation (short):
- Identify artifact and repo; rotate any cloud credentials that appear in the artifact immediately.
- Rebuild artifact without embedding secrets (use env vars or vault integration).
- Sign artifact with cosign/sigstore and push.
- Update CI to use ephemeral credentials (OIDC) and add owner metadata to publish step.

ci-bot: quick examples: rotate AWS key: `aws iam create-access-key --user-name ci-user && aws iam delete-access-key --access-key-id OLDKEY`. GCP: create new SA key with `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create new.json --iam-account=sa@example.com` and delete old. Azure: `az ad app credential reset --id <APP_ID>`. Update pipeline secrets in Vault.

pj.platform: is there a helper to rewrite artifacts to strip secrets retroactively?

anya.sec: We cannot safely scrub some binary checkpoints. For a few small archives we can do an advisory rewrite (contact sec-automations). For model checkpoints, rebuild is recommended. We will not automatically modify published artifacts.

ops-lead: timeline for enforcement?

anya.sec: Timeline: owner notification and CSVs out 2026-08-10; rotation & re-push recommended by 2026-08-24; policy enablement (quarantine unsigned/flagged artifacts) 2026-09-01. We'll run a dry-run mode 2026-08-25 to report expected quarantines without blocking pulls.

artifact-bot: dry-run report scheduled for 2026-08-25.

anya.sec: Exceptions: file `sec-exception:artifact` with justification and expiry; exceptions are limited and reviewed by GRC. For urgent help, contact sec-automations@redwood.com with `artifact` in the subject.

pj.platform: noted, will schedule a rotation sprint and add cosign step to our release pipeline.

ops-lead: please DM the per-team lists when ready.

anya.sec: Summary/checklist:
- Run CSV export and identify impacted artifacts.
- Rotate any confirmed cloud creds found in artifacts immediately.
- Rebuild and sign artifacts, add owner metadata.
- Monitor dry-run report 2026-08-25 and fix before 2026-09-01 enforcement.

anya.sec: We'll post progress pings here and in #platform. If you want your team's report sooner ping me or DM artifact-bot. :lock:
